text.p: Grain and oilseed exports reported by USDA and private export sources.

CORN SALE - South Korea's National Livestock Cooperatives Federation bought a total of 210,000 tonnes of No. 3 Chinese, Argentine and U.S. corn and passed on 52,500 tonnes due to high prices, traders said. Shipment dates for the corn purchases ranged from March 1 through July 10.

CORN/SOYBEAN SALE - Taiwan Sugar Corp bought 20,000 tonnes of U.S. corn and 10,000 tonnes of U.S. soybeans from Mitsui, traders said. Shipment is slated from the U.S. Pacific Northwest for March 10 to 25.

CORN SALE - Taiwan's Members Feed Industry bought 54,000 tonnes of U.S. No.2 corn from Garnac, traders said. Half was priced at $143.50 per tonne and half at 94.8 cents over Chicago May futures, both C and F. Shipment is from the U.S. Gulf March 8-22 or the Pacific Northwest March 23-April 6, traders said.
WHEAT TENDERS - India's state-run trading corporation will tender for 50,000 tonnes of wheat for arrival by the end of March. The tender will close on January 29.
- Jordan will tender on February 5 for 50,000 tonnes of U.S. hard wheat or equivalent origin for shipment by March 31, traders said. U.S. wheat would be under the GSM 102 program.

WHEAT TENDER - Moroccan importers will buy a total of 27,000 tonnes of optional-origin milling wheat, traders said. One tender for 12,000 tonnes is set January 21, with delivery slated for January 31. A second tender will be held for 15,000 tonnes on January 23. Shipment for that purchase is set for February 25 through March 5, traders and export sources said.
- Lebanon's economy ministry plans to buy 50,000 tonnes of U.S. hard wheat later this month, the government said.
- Results were awaited on Bangladesh's tender for 100,000 tonnes of U.S. No.2 wheat or Australian or Canadian winter red/spring wheat for shipment by February 21.

BARLEY/WHEAT TENDER - The Cyprus Grain Commission invited tenders for one shipment of 12,000 tonnes of European milling wheat and one 25,000 tonne shipment of barley. Shipment was March 13-28 for the wheat and February for the barley.
CORN TENDER - News was awaited on South Africa's Maize Board's tender for 15,000 tonnes of yellow maize for either export or domestic use. The offer was seen closing January 16.
RICE TENDER - Syria's General Foreign Trade Organization for Chemicals and Foodstuffs is seeking to buy 12,000 tonnes of white rice for March shipment. Results would be February 13.

SOYBEAN TENDER - South Korea's state-run Agricultural and Fishery Marketing Corp invited tenders for 40,000 tonnes of U.S. No. 1 soybeans on January 29. Shipment of one 20,000 purchase will be for January 30 to February 18 from the U.S. Gulf or from February 14 to March 5 from the U.S. Pacific Northwest. Shipment of the other 20,000 tonnes will be from the U.S. Gulf between February 24 to March 15 or from PNW March 11 to 30.
MARKET TALK - The Australian Wheat Board expects to sell another 100,000 tonnes of wheat to Iraq under that country's food-for-oil program, an AWB spokesman said.

- Iraq was said to have purchased between 300,000 and 325,000 tonnes of French wheat for March-April shipment, but the deal was yet to be confirmed, traders said. Exporters cited a selling price of $185.75 per tonne, C and F, for delivery to Umm Qasr and $219.00 per tonne for Baghdad delivery, traders said.
